scenes.title: Articulated porcelain infant macaque anchoring its hind feet on the terrycloth surrogate while leaning across to nurse from the bare wire frame
scenes.era: 1958, University of Wisconsin Primate Laboratory, Madison

layout.description: Brightly lit 1958 observation chamber with glass viewing window, containing two side-by-side inclined cylindrical surrogates: on the left, bare silver welded wire mesh holding a glass milk bottle; on the right, warm tan cushioned terrycloth with no bottle.

positions.who: Articulated matte-white porcelain infant macaque sculpture
positions.where: anchoring both hind feet tightly onto the soft tan terrycloth cylinder while stretching its arms sideways across the gap to sip from the wire frame's bottle
positions.facing: bridging from cloth surrogate toward wire bottle

positions.who: Harry Harlow (mannequin in 1950s white lab coat and horn-rimmed glasses)
positions.where: standing outside the glass observation window with a dual-channel timer clock logging hours on cloth versus wire

props.name: bare welded-wire milk surrogate
props.period_detail: inclined cylindrical wire-mesh frame fitted with a single glass nursing bottle at chest height
props.physical_behavior: logged at under 1.5 hours of contact per day despite holding all food

props.name: soft tan terrycloth surrogate
props.period_detail: identical inclined cylinder wrapped in cushioned sponge rubber and textured tan terrycloth towel fabric
props.physical_behavior: logged at 17+ hours of daily clinging contact despite zero milk

props.name: dual electromechanical contact-time clocks
props.period_detail: two 1950s dial counters wired to pressure switches under each surrogate base
props.physical_behavior: cloth clock reads 17 hours while wire clock barely passes 1 hour

actions.verb_sequence: clings tightly to the tan terrycloth cylinder -> keeps hind feet locked on the soft cloth while leaning across to drink briefly from the wire bottle -> snaps immediately back onto the terrycloth chest
points to the 17-hour vs 1-hour counter dials outside the glass window

reactions.reaction: rests calmly against the textured tan terrycloth once hunger is satisfied
notes how tactile contact completely overrides food reinforcement

scenes.wardrobe: Experimenter mannequin in 1958 white cotton lab coat, collared shirt, and narrow tie; animal subject strictly rendered as an articulated matte-white porcelain infant macaque sculpture.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1958 laboratory daylight illuminating the stark texture contrast between cold silver wire mesh and warm tan terrycloth.
scenes.recognition_hook: Keeping both feet locked onto the milkless soft terrycloth surrogate, the porcelain infant stretches sideways just long enough to sip from the bare wire bottle before snapping right back to the cloth.

key_visual.description: an articulated matte-white porcelain infant macaque anchoring its feet on a tan terrycloth cylinder while leaning sideways to drink from an adjacent bare wire-mesh frame with a bottle

scenes.title: Mechanical drumming toy triggers an instant sprint to the cloth surrogate

layout.description: Clean testing enclosure containing both wire and cloth surrogates as a small wind-up toy bear with a miniature drum sits at the opposite end.

positions.where: sprinting straight past the bare wire milk frame to clasp the tan terrycloth surrogate tightly

props.name: wind-up drumming toy
props.period_detail: small 1950s tin mechanical toy holding two tiny drumsticks
props.physical_behavior: triggers an immediate flight toward the cloth haven

actions.verb_sequence: sets down the tin drumming toy -> porcelain infant darts past the wire feeder and leaps onto the terrycloth cylinder

reactions.reaction: calms down against the cloth, then turns its head curiously back toward the toy

scenes.wardrobe: 1958 lab coat; articulated porcelain macaque sculpture.
scenes.recognition_hook: Under sudden fear, even wire-fed infants run past their food source straight to the soft cloth mother.

scenes.title: Open-field room exploration using the cloth mother as a secure base

layout.description: Spacious white testing room scattered with wooden blocks, folded paper, and a small climbing cube around the central tan terrycloth surrogate.

positions.where: stepping bravely out from the terrycloth base to inspect a wooden block, glancing back once for reassurance

props.name: wooden curiosity blocks
props.period_detail: colorful geometric blocks arranged across the floor
props.physical_behavior: explored freely only when the cloth surrogate stands in the room

actions.verb_sequence: touches the cloth base -> walks out three steps to pick up a wooden cube

reactions.reaction: charts exploratory steps rising dramatically when the secure base is present

scenes.recognition_hook: With a warm safe base in the room, fear turns into bold exploration.

scenes.title: Modern hospital kangaroo skin-to-skin newborn care

layout.description: Sunlit modern hospital room where a parent mannequin holds a swaddled newborn calmly against their chest while vital-sign monitors show steady waves.

positions.who: Parent mannequin in soft cotton wrap
positions.where: reclining calmly in an armchair holding infant close

props.name: vital-sign bedside monitor
props.period_detail: clean medical display showing steady calm heart-rate trace

actions.verb_sequence: places warm blanket gently over parent and infant

reactions.reaction: relaxes as the monitor trace steadies

scenes.wardrobe: Soft modern hospital wrap and scrubs.
scenes.recognition_hook: Harlow's contact-comfort proof helped overturn no-touch nursery rules in favor of skin-to-skin care.
